I built a high-performance file copier for ML datasets using Linux io_uring. On the right workload, it's 4.2x faster than cp -r. Here's what I learned about when async I/O helps—and when it doesn't. ML training datasets often contain millions of small files:
Dataset Files Typical Size
ImageNet 1.28M 100-200KB JPEG
COCO 330K 50-500KB
MNIST 70K 784 bytes
CIFAR-10 60K 3KB
Copying these with cp -r is painfully slow. Each file requires multiple syscalls (open, read, write, close), and the kernel processes them one at a time.
